examples: I'm very interested in Korean culture.
Culture is different in each country.
Food is also a part of culture.
nuance: 문화 (culture) covers customs, arts, and ways of life. It often combines into compounds like 문화 차이 (cultural difference), 대중문화 (pop culture), and 문화재 (cultural heritage).
mistakes: Do not confuse 문화 (culture) with 문학 (literature) — they look similar but mean different things.

examples: 그 영화를 보고 정말 감동을 받았어요.
I was really moved after watching that movie.
I was touched by the teacher's letter.
nuance: 감동 is the warm, moved feeling you get from something touching. Use 감동을 받다 (to be moved), 감동을 주다 (to move someone), and the adjective 감동적이다 (moving/touching).
mistakes: 감동하다 means 'to be moved', not 'to move an object' — for that use 옮기다/움직이다.

examples: This restaurant has a diverse menu.
I want to try various experiences.
nuance: 다양하다 (various/diverse) describes a wide range of types or options. The modifier is 다양한 N and the adverb is 다양하게. A close word is 여러 (several), but 다양하다 stresses variety, not just number.
mistakes: Modifier is 다양한, not 다양하는 (it is an adjective, so 다양한 N).
